audit.whatIsWrong: Every field tells the player to track Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining cooldown. Scrap Shield is a flat 6 seconds and is effectively always available. The real limiter is Heat, and Overheating is never mentioned once.
audit.why: Riot text, Junkyard Titan: 'Every spell Rumble casts gives him Heat. When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells for [a duration].' Scrap Shield cooldown is 6s. A Rumble at 100 Heat cannot cast Flamespitter, Scrap Shield or Electro Harpoon at all — that is a hard, readable, repeating window that no cooldown timer gives you.
audit.corrected: Fight on his Heat bar. At 100 Heat he is locked out of every spell — Body Slam in there. Scrap Shield returning every 6 seconds is never a window worth waiting for.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is described only as a slow. It also reduces Magic Resist, and he carries two charges.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Rumble launches a harpoon, electrocuting his target with magic damage, slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist. Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time.' Range 850, recharge 0.5s between casts. Two harpoons in you means your bought MR is partly stripped before his Flamespitter lands — which changes how much Mercury's Treads and MR actually buy you.
audit.corrected: Two harpoons shred your MR before the fire lands, so pair MR with raw HP rather than stacking resistances alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty 6/10 against a 55.56% Emerald+ win rate over 234 games with Gragas holding five of seven stages.
audit.why: The packet chart gives Gragas Levels 2 through first item outright. This is a favourable lane, not an even one.
audit.corrected: Difficulty set to 4/10, framed as fighting on his Heat bar rather than on a 6-second shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven level-chart sides contradicted the packet chart and the content layer's own why text.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Skill. Stored sides were Skill, Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Skill, Rumble, Rumble, while whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Gragas winning those stages ('out-heal his Flamespitter poke', 'you out-trade his harpoon-and-fire poke', 'E-W-Q plus Explosive Cask all-in beats him').
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Skill in both layers with ratings to match, as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The range gap that makes the level-1 stand-off readable is never stated.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is 850 range; Flamespitter is a 600-range cone lasting 3 seconds. You can poke from outside his damage entirely.
audit.corrected: Poke from 850 and never step inside 600 while his Heat is low.

audit.why: All four packet suspectNames are false positives: 'Electro Harpoon', 'The Equalizer', 'Drunken Rage' and 'Flamespitter' are the real ability names, flagged only because the surrounding words ('Land', 'Drop', possessive 's, 'His') shifted the edit distance. No name edits made.

notes: The full layer told the player to build the entire lane around Scrap Shield, a 6-second cooldown that is always up — structurally the same error the mirror audit (rumble__gragas) found with Drunken Rage's flat 5s. Replaced throughout with the Heat bar: at 100% Heat Rumble Overheats and cannot cast any spell, which is the only real commit window in this matchup and appeared nowhere on the page. Also added Electro Harpoon's Magic Resist shred (2 charges, 850 range) — it was described only as a slow, and it directly undercuts the page's own 'build MR' advice, so the itemization line now pairs MR with health. Level chart was inverted in six of seven rows. All four packet suspectNames are false positives and were left alone. One inconsistency I did not resolve: the packet chart calls Level 1 'Skill' while whys[0] and spikes[0] both say the level is Rumble's — I followed the packet and wrote phases[0].why to sit honestly between the two, but the content whys[0] text still leans Rumble; see questionsForUser.
